content: Rilpivirine should be used with caution when co-administered with drugs that are known to prolong the QTc interval, as this combination may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. Close monitoring is recommended in such cases. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of artemether/lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised during co-administration. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised during co-administration. Both asenapine (transdermal) and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these agents are used together. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. If antacids must be administered, they should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours afterward. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended during co-administration. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these agents are used together. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes and/or sudden death. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal.
